name: Content moderation

subjectOf.text: Popularity based ranking cannot substitute for editorial control, because people end up relying on unconscious algorithms to determine what is authoritative and the Folk Theorems establish that such algorithms can always be gamed.
subjectOf.abstract: People rely on unconscious algorithms which use popularity to determine what is authoritative content. But the lessons of the Folk Theorems again arise, to remind us that such algorithms can always be gamed.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of History In Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782217
scope_conditions: user generated content platforms without editorial control

subjectOf.text: Web3 systems answer the web2 pathology at the architectural level rather than the content level: decentralized, transparent, community governed designs eliminate the centralized control that drives misinformation and echo chambers, and substitute transparency, decentralization, and user control.
subjectOf.abstract: Unlike Web2 platforms, Web3 systems aim to eliminate the centralized control that exacerbates the spread of misinformation and the creation of echo chambers. Instead, they prioritize transparency, decentralization, and user control,
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Future of Law - Dynamic Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4957318
scope_conditions: decentralized and community governed platform architectures

subjectOf.text: Decentralized data production will succeed only if it solves fraudulent submissions, content moderation, and alignment with ethical and legal frameworks; these are necessary conditions, not incidental risks.
subjectOf.abstract: their success critically depends on addressing challenges such as fraudulent submissions, content moderation, and ensuring alignment with ethical and legal frameworks.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
